about.what: Level 2 of the measured grid (tools/learn_check.py): every cell trained for 250 iterations under the settings below and compared with the method as shipped under the same settings. One run per cell; a statement about training dynamics on 8 frames of one scene, not an accuracy measurement. See docs/advanced_guides/learns_like_reference.md.

outcomes.fails: the run did not finish: an exception, a crash, a timeout, or no real frame read. A run that died of GPU memory is not recorded (it says nothing about the config) and is run again
outcomes.no reference: the method as shipped has no finished run under the same settings: nothing to compare with
outcomes.diverging: a loss term is rising over the last half of the run (see `rising`), a loss or a weight became non-finite, or no grasp was predicted on any of the 4 frames while the reference predicts some
outcomes.worse: not diverging, and a comparable loss term ends above the tolerance of the method times the reference's (mean of the last 25 iterations), or a part of the model that holds trainable parameters received no gradient in any iteration
outcomes.not comparable: not diverging, nothing worse, but the cell changes the definition of every term the reference has: there is no term to compare
outcomes.on a par: every comparable loss term ends within the tolerance of the method, at least one term is comparable, nothing rises, every value is finite and a frame has a grasp. A term far below the reference's is reported (`lower`), not judged

measures.mean: the mean of a loss term over the last 25 of the 250 iterations (reported, finite values; the total `loss` is not judged, it sums terms whose definitions may differ)
measures.ratio: the cell's mean divided by the reference's mean of the same term
measures.rise: over the last half of the run (iterations 126 to 250), the mean of its second half divided by the mean of its first half, minus 1 (the middle iteration of an odd count in neither half): +0.30 means the term ended 30 % higher than it was half-way
measures.tolerance: per method: 1.25, or the first multiple of 0.05 above the largest ratio between two seeds of its reference (any term but the total, either way round), when that is larger
measures.rising: a rise above the rising threshold of the method that also exceeds the reference's rise of the term by more than it (the rise alone for a term the reference does not report); the threshold is 0.1, or the first multiple of 0.05 above the largest difference between the rises of one term under two seeds of the reference, when that is larger
measures.lower: a comparable term below 1/tolerance of the reference's: reported, not judged

not_comparable.loss: a loss preset replaces the function of the term it is put in
not_comparable.head: a head bundle defines the targets and the loss of every head term (score, width, angle, depth, tolerance)
not_comparable.assigner: an assigner changes the labels the view stage and the head see (a view stage sees the labels through the assigner only): every view and head term
not_comparable.stage code: a proposal or view stage owns its targets and its loss: one whose class computes them with other code (its own `loss` or target methods, not inherited from the reference's stage) defines every term of that stage anew; one that computes them as the reference's does, with the same loss options, keeps them (a proposal that changes only how it samples)
not_comparable.presence: a term only one of the two runs reports
not_comparable.sign: a term whose mean is not positive (a weighted loss can go below zero)

about.calibration: A cell and its reference are two runs, so a ratio away from 1 means something only beyond what two runs of the very same config show. Every reference was therefore trained twice, under seed 0 and seed 1 (*The noise floor*). Under the five seed-based methods, a term that has settled (it rose or fell by less than 10 % over the last half) agrees within 7 % between the seeds; a term still falling steeply at the end differs more (EconomicGrasp's graspness by 1.32x), and HGGD at its peak rate differs by up to 1.55x (angle, offsets). One tolerance for all would be blind under the stable methods or trigger-happy under HGGD, so each method gets its own: 1.25 (the plan's value, more than three times the spread of a settled term) unless its references spread more, then the first multiple of 0.05 above their largest ratio. The rising threshold follows the same rule from the rises. The spread comes from one pair of runs per method: a third seed would firm it up

fields.id, kind, method: the cell of the grid (tools/probe_grid.py), its kind (KINDS) and method
fields.option: the slot=choice pairs of its compose request
fields.outcome, reasons: the outcome (about.outcomes) and what decided it
fields.notes: what is reported, not judged: lower terms, a level-2 run that is runs-unstable for another reason than a non-finite value, no grasp as for the reference
fields.terms: per loss term: [cell's mean, reference's mean, ratio] over the last window, or the reason it is not comparable (about.not_comparable)
fields.rise: per loss term: its rise over the last half of the run (about.measures)
fields.grasps_per_frame, score_median: grasps predicted on each of the predicted frames, and the median score of each (null for a frame without a grasp)
fields.constant_scores: true when every predicted grasp of a frame has the same score, on every frame with a grasp: the score head ignores its input
fields.no_gradient, unchanged, checked: units without a gradient, parts whose weights did not change, and [units, parts] checked (grasppanda.combine.probe.JUDGE_FIELDS)
fields.schedule, rate: how the probe set the learning rate: `constant` at `rate` (the recipe's peak, scaled to the batch), or `recipe` for a cell whose request sets the schedule
fields.probe, compose, config_hash, run: the commands, the config hash (with the seed for a seeded run) and the run that measured it (about.runs)
fields.seconds: wall time of the probe, measured on a shared machine

left_out.post: post-processing trains nothing, so a training run says nothing about it; its check is to compare the grasps in and out of the chain (and the evaluator) on 20 frames of a trained method, which is not part of this page yet
left_out.stage-set, cross: several slots replaced at once: no single stage of the reference to compare with
